headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem while aci can route CRM/email/calendar data through broad network egress, creating dangerous leakage and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can emit content into email, Slack, Notion, Sheets, CRM, or MCP-style flows, while B reads the filesystem, clipboard, and stdin/stdout by default. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if A’s outputs are copied into files or prompts that B consumes. The pathway is not provably blocked in either profile.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into a file, clipboard, or stdin that B parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF B is run with auto-run or similar reduced-confirmation mode, malicious instructions in A’s output can be executed.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces/filesystems.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Require manual review of A’s outputs before B consumes them.
Run B without auto-run and keep per-command confirmation enabled.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all A-to-B handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data, and B has broad filesystem read/write plus broad network egress. If A’s outputs or synced files land in B’s workspace, B can exfiltrate sensitive business data to third-party model providers or other endpoints. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible and not safely contained.
conditions: IF A writes CRM/email/calendar artifacts into a shared directory, B can read them.
IF B sends its context or file contents to configured model providers, those data can leave the local machine.
mitigations: Use separate OS users for A and B.
Mount B on a restricted directory with no CRM/email exports.
Disable network egress for B when handling A-derived files.
Redact sensitive fields before any A-to-B transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; A can also operate through APIs and MCP-style integrations. If both touch the same repo, workspace, or synced files, concurrent writes and state corruption are plausible, and git changes can be overwritten or committed incorrectly. No locking or coordination primitive is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF A and B operate on the same repository or shared directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF B modifies git state while A is generating or syncing artifacts, state corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Use git branches per agent and merge manually.
Disable concurrent runs against the same repo.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce CRM/email/calendar actions and B can execute shell commands and filesystem changes. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious A output can cascade into irreversible external actions or local destructive changes. The profiles do not show a verification gate that would reliably stop this.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as instructions or facts without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF A’s output includes a destructive command or incorrect CRM/email action and B executes it, the error cascades.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source data.
Block direct execution of A-generated shell commands.
Use a human approval step for any external side effect.
Limit A to draft-only outputs for B.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data, while B can access anything reachable on the local machine and has broad filesystem/network access. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for retention, residency, and subject-rights handling if regulated data is placed in B’s workspace. The profiles do not show matching controls or a DPA boundary.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied from A into B’s local filesystem, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF EU or other restricted data is processed by B without a documented transfer basis, residency/compliance issues arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B’s workspace.
Use a documented data-transfer policy between agents.
Delete B-side artifacts immediately after use.
Restrict B to synthetic or anonymized inputs.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement controls.
